title: Security-assistance proposals often lacked documented partner absorption, sustainment, or measurable objectives
source_unit: 46 selected Department of Defense Section 333 train-and-equip project proposals notified to Congress in fiscal years 2018–2021
geography: United States security-cooperation system and foreign partner projects; DOD geographic combatant commands and five overseas posts

observations.period: Fiscal years 2018–2022 allocations and FY2018–2021 selected proposals; GAO-23-105842, August 2023; recommendation follow-up current through April 2026

denominator.unit: selected Section 333 project proposals reviewed by GAO; nongeneralizable sample

planning_gap.unit: proposals that did not fully document a sustainment plan, partner absorptive-capacity analysis, or measurable objectives

section_333_allocation.unit: billion U.S. dollars allocated to Section 333 projects in fiscal years 2018–2022

state_involvement.value: State participation varied and often occurred later in the proposal process; GAO found no defined joint DOD–State planning process as of March 2026

project_success_boundary.value: assistance may be provided that partner nations cannot use or sustain
project_success_boundary.unit: reported implementation risk, not observed universal failure

recommendation_status.value: recommendations on joint process, guidance, and detailed absorptive-capacity notifications remained open in the April 2026 follow-up described by GAO

observations.method: GAO review of program guidance, project proposals, congressional notifications, allocation data, and interviews with DOD and State officials at headquarters, six geographic combatant commands, and five overseas posts; the proposal sample was selected for review and is not generalizable to all projects.
observations.uncertainty: The review does not estimate the share of all Section 333 projects that failed, does not follow the 46 proposals to delivery or partner use, and does not measure partner-side capability, operational effect, local legitimacy, or adversary response. The $5.6 billion is a program allocation total, not the value of the 46 reviewed proposals or evidence of delivered capability.
observations.subgroup: Selected Section 333 proposals and the DOD/State planning offices, combatant commands, and overseas posts involved in their review; partner countries are represented through planning requirements rather than matched outcome observations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Incomplete proposal documentation can reflect reporting or process failure rather than unusable assistance; some partners may absorb and sustain capabilities despite weak documentation, and later guidance or templates may improve future proposals. Conversely, a completed planning template still would not prove delivery, use, readiness, or strategic effect.

related_sources.claim: GAO's later international-arrangements review supplies a separate agreement-level coordination and oversight comparator
GAO recommendation follow-up reports current DOD and State implementation status

boundary: This record adds a security-assistance planning and partner-capacity stage between authorization/funding and delivered or jointly used capability. It does not establish that Section 333 assistance failed, that a specific partner lacked capability, or that U.S. security cooperation changed deterrence, alliance behavior, or adversary choices.
